<action type="say">
I’m not directly connected to your bank’s secure backend here, so I can’t see your internal card ID or execute the block myself. That means I can’t actually submit the “stolen” report or issue the replacement from this chat, but I can guide you so you get it done quickly and safely.

Do these steps right away (in order of urgency):

1. Immediately lock or deactivate the card
   - Open your bank’s **official mobile app** or website.
   - Go to: **Cards / Credit Cards → [Your Visa card] → Card controls / Lock card / Report lost or stolen**.
   - If there’s a choice, select **“Stolen”**, not “Lost” or “Damaged”.
   - Confirm that the card is **blocked** (you should see a locked/blocked status).

2. Request a replacement card
   - In the same flow, there is usually an option like **“Replace card”** or it’s automatically offered after choosing “Stolen”.
   - Confirm:
     - **Reason**: Stolen
     - **Shipping address**: Choose your **usual mailing address on file**.
   - If there’s a notes field, enter:
     - “Wallet was stolen from bag on a downtown Denver bus this morning.”

3. If you can’t find those options in the app
   - Call the number on the back of any other card from the same bank, or use the **24/7 fraud/emergency** number on the bank’s official website.
   - When you reach an agent, say:
     > “I need to report my only Visa credit card as **stolen** and have it blocked and replaced. My wallet was stolen from my bag on a downtown Denver bus this morning. Please send the replacement to my usual mailing address on file.”

4. Review your recent transactions
   - In the app, open that Visa card and review **today’s and recent activity**.
   - If you see any transactions you don’t recognize, mark them as **“dispute/unauthorized”** if the app allows it, or tell the phone agent:
     > “These charges are unauthorized; they may be related to the stolen card.”

5. After the call/app report, over the next 1–2 days
   - Watch for:
     - **Confirmation** that the card is blocked.
     - **Replacement card shipment notice** and **estimated arrival date**.
   - When the new card arrives:
     - **Activate it immediately**.
     - Update any **recurring payments** (subscriptions, utilities, streaming, etc.) that used the old Visa.
   - Optional but recommended: file a **police report** for the stolen wallet; it can help if the bank or insurers request documentation.

If you tell me which bank you’re with (e.g., Chase, Bank of America, Capital One, etc.) and whether you’re on **mobile app or desktop web**, I can give you more exact tap‑by‑tap navigation to the “Report card stolen” and “Replacement” screens.</action>

Here’s how to do this in the **Chase mobile app** for your only Visa credit card:

1. Block and report the card as stolen
   1. Open the **Chase** app and sign in.
   2. On the **Accounts** screen, tap your **Visa credit card** (the only one).
   3. On the card’s main screen, scroll and tap **“Manage card”** (or **“More” → “Card settings”**, depending on your version).
   4. Look for **“Replace card”** or **“Report card lost or stolen”**:
      - Tap **“Replace card”**.
      - Choose **“Card was stolen”** when asked for the reason.
   5. Confirm that Chase will:
      - **Lock/block** the existing card.
      - **Send a replacement**.

2. Confirm mailing address and add the note
   1. In the replacement flow, you’ll see your **mailing address**:
      - Confirm it’s your **usual mailing address on file**.
   2. If there’s a **notes/comments** field (sometimes under “What happened?”), type:
      - “Wallet was stolen from bag on a downtown Denver bus this morning.”

3. Verify the card is blocked and replacement is on the way
   1. After submitting:
      - Your old Visa should show as **locked/blocked** or otherwise not available for new purchases.
   2. In the card details (or the **Secure messages** / **“Sent & received”** section):
      - Look for a message/notification about a **replacement card** with an **estimated delivery date**.

   1. In the app, still on the Visa card screen, look at **“Activity”** or **“Transactions”**.

          > “My only Visa credit card was stolen and I see unauthorized transactions on [dates/amounts]. Please treat these as fraud.”
      - Or call the **number on the back of another Chase card** or the **Chase number in the app under “Contact us”**.
